newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says to bolster Philippines trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says to bolster Philippines trade ties.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister said on Tuesday the island would strengthen trade and investment with the Philippines following a secret four-day visit billed as a private vacation he made to the southeast Asian nation.
Foreign Minister John Chang told reporters he met "important figures" during his visit to the Philippines, but declined to give names or details.
The Philippines maintains diplomatic ties only with communist China and not with Nationalist-ruled Taiwan, which is regarded by Beijing as a renegade province.

"Our current diplomatic position makes it very difficult to have the opportunity to meet those friends," Chang said of his Philippine hosts. "I have promised them not to reveal any details. I need to keep that promise."
Chang said, however, the visit helped to promote business links and regional cooperation. He did not elaborate.
Beijing maintains that Taiwan is ineligible for sovereign foreign relations and demands that other countries end links with the island if they want diplomatic ties with China.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
To evade China's diplomatic embargo, Taiwan officials have engaged in "pragmatic diplomacy" -- quiet, unofficial visits to countries that recognise Beijing instead of Taipei.
Chang and Vice-President Lien Chan have between them visited the Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, Belgium, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the past two years in similar trips veiled in secrecy.
South Africa, Taiwan's largest ally, dealt Taipei a shock in November by announcing that it would cut diplomatic ties with the island and recognise Beijing in 1997.
